objective: Create reproducible versioned offline Software Factory bundles and verify bundle contents/compatibility against an independent publisher-authorized, externally provisioned digest and release identity; emit a pinned installation lock, without silent upgrades or release claims.
nonGoals: No autonomous publication, network upload, GitHub release creation, installation into other repositories, or deployments
No self-authenticating embedded checksums or unsupported claim that a locally created trust file proves publisher identity
No bespoke cryptographic signature primitive or implied SLSA provenance certification
No weakening CI, permission, merge queue or other repository controls
No alteration of existing install/upgrade/removal behavior or target files
decisions: Use deterministic archive and trusted digest pin provisioned out of band; a matching self-embedded checksum is never authentication; signed provenance remains a separately qualifying extension.

obligations.description: Build reproducible offline archive from clean committed Git source with exact allowed portable paths, sorted canonical manifest, explicit version/source identity and bounded contents.
Reject tampered, untrusted, mismatched, corrupt, missing, duplicate, traversal, symlink, oversized and unsupported bundles; require out-of-band trusted publisher/release/digest policy.
Verify version/schema compatibility, produce deterministic project-installation lock only when explicitly requested, without overwriting or auto-updating.
Preserve Windows/Linux behavior; offline no-network operation and minimal dependency footprint; no implicit release/merge claim.
Prepare full SF-08 through SF-13 cumulative diff and verify PR #22 required checks and merge-queue prerequisites while preserving authorization boundary.

structure: src/sf/distribution.py: deterministic archive builder, strict manifest verifier, externally trusted digest policy and lock writer
src/sf/cli.py: explicit sf distribution build/verify CLI
tests/test_distribution.py: synthetic Git repos, binary tamper, dangerous ZIP and compatibility fixtures
docs/factory/SF13_DISTRIBUTION.md: distribution trust, manual issuance and update/removal compatibility contracts
impact: Adds opt-in offline package verification without modifying target repository files or accepting self-signed candidate output
Archive contains only project-agnostic factory runtime/contracts and skills, never historical bot evidence
PR #22 contains full stack to main but merge execution remains separately authorized

budget.network: None for local build and verification; single stable PR validation and required queue later
budget.execution: Focused offline tests, stable Linux/Windows PR acceptance once, no redundant Actions reruns

externalEffects: User requested preparation of merge after PR #22; do not enter merge queue or merge without separate explicit go-ahead
Do not deploy, distribute publicly, install into other projects or publish releases
Do not change settings, CI workflows, or repositories other than spsoftwarefc/s-f
